children: Wall Street’s major averages pushed higher Friday after the latest consumer inflation report came in largely in line with expectations.
Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:
Consumer Price Index rises 0.4% in August:

0.4% month-over-month in August, matching consensus, while the year-over-year reading held steady at 3.4%. Gasoline prices rose 3.9% during the month, accounting for over one-third of the overall increase, while shelter costs climbed 0.3%. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, came in above expectations at 0.3% month-over-month, translating to 2.4% annual growth. Analysts say the data effectively seals a Federal Reserve rate hike at next week's meeting, with markets now pricing in possibly four total hikes ahead.
Record diesel prices heighten energy inflation fears:

above $6 a gallon for the first time on record, with the national average reaching $6.0556 according to the American Automobile Association—and approaching $8 in California. The spike follows U.S. crude futures topping $100 a barrel on Thursday for the first time since May, up roughly 20% in September amid escalating U.S.-Iran hostilities. The timing presents political challenges with just over 50 days until midterm elections, particularly in heating-oil-dependent states like Maine and agricultural states such as Ohio, Kansas, and Iowa.
Tech hardware shares surge on AI demand and PC refresh:

8% or more in Friday morning trading, driven by sustained enterprise AI demand and an anticipated PC refresh cycle. HPE received an additional boost from Oracle's strong earnings results and a new partnership under which Oracle will deploy HPE's routing and switching platforms across all its data centers as it scales global AI infrastructure. RBC Capital Markets initiated coverage on Dell with an Outperform rating and $640 price target, noting the company exited Q2 with a $95 billion AI server backlog.
Leopold Aschenbrenner's AI fund resumes bullish options bets:

Situational Awareness, the artificial-intelligence-focused hedge fund founded by former OpenAI researcher Leopold Aschenbrenner, has  returned to active trading through call option purchases after nearly collapsing in late July. The fund has been buying positions in AMD, Bloom Energy, Coreweave, SK Hynix, and Sandisk, with purchases totaling hundreds of millions of dollars in premium made last week and early this week.
